verdict.rationale: GitHub's fine-grained personal access tokens let a user scope permissions to specific resources and see required permissions via the X-Accepted-GitHub-Permissions header, which directly supports issuing least-privilege credentials that could be used for an agent (e.g., an AI coding agent using the API). However, the evidence doesn't explicitly frame this as agent-specific credentialing (no mention of Copilot/agent-specific token scoping workflows, token expiration/rotation best practices, or agent-specific OAuth app scoping). missing for 10: agent-specific credential issuance workflow, documentation tying fine-grained PATs explicitly to AI agent use cases, independent/hands-on corroboration of scoping in practice.
